name: Verne Eighty
lines: Around the World in Eighty Days
Jules Verne · Around the World in Eighty Days (1872), translated by George Makepeace Towle (1873), the whole book
No. 7, Saville Row, London (the Pall Mall book)
The British consulate, Suez
🕰️ The port clock of Suez: two hours ahead of London. Passepartout's watch will not believe it.
The shop for shirts and shoes
👞 A little shop under an awning: shirts, socks, Indian slippers, a hat or two. The shopkeeper bows you in.
Boat, sir? To the steamer, quick, quick!
A coal-heaver of the port
Four hours to coal her. She burns a mountain between here and Aden.
G. I. P. RAILWAY · BOMBAY
The railway station
🚂 Bori Bunder station: the night train for Allahabad and Calcutta, eight o'clock. Passengers, porters, a sacred cow that walks where it likes.
The passport office
📜 The passport office: a clerk with a pen, a fan turning overhead, a stamp.
The pagoda on Malabar Hill
go in (take off your shoes!)
look at the stalls
🌶️ Turmeric, cardamom, chillies, cotton cloth, brass and copper pots, sugar cane: and every voice in Bombay bargaining at once.
A porter of the station
The Calcutta train, sahib? Eight o'clock. All the way, they say.
A Parsee merchant of Bombay
Welcome to Bombay. The canal has brought all Europe to our door.
The end of the rails
🛤️ The rails stop here, in the middle of a forest of dates and acacias. Fifty miles still to lay to Allahabad.
A workman of the railway
Fifty miles more, sahib. Next year, perhaps.
The forest of Bundelcund
The pagoda of Pillaji
go in (by night, quietly)
The pyre in the glade
🔥 A pile of sandal-wood, already soaked with perfumed oil. At dawn the priests will light it.
🪵 A great pile of sandal-wood in the glade. At dawn the priests mean to finish their dreadful rite here; you mean to stop them.
The thicket at the edge of the glade
🌿 Under the trees, in the dark, five hundred paces from the pagoda. Nobody sees you.
ALLAHABAD · E. I. RAILWAY
🚂 Allahabad: the line begins again here, east to Benares and Calcutta. Where the Ganges and the Jumna meet, the most sacred meeting of rivers in India.
🌊 Steps down to the Hooghly: bathers, washermen, boats with high prows, and the steamers for Hong Kong lying in the stream.
A boatman of the Hooghly
The Rangoon sails at noon, sahib. Noon exactly.
🏨 The Club Hotel: verandas, punkahs, an English dinner, and a list of the steamers on the wall.
A tavern on the quay
The wharf of the pilot-boats
⛵ The Tankadere, pilot-boat No. 43, twenty tons, a pretty schooner with all her sails furled: "the best in the harbour".
A Chinese shopkeeper of Victoria
Good tea, good silk, good price. Come in, come in.
A sailor of the harbour
The Carnatic? Repairing her boiler. Off tomorrow morning, they say.
⛩️ A great red gate; beyond it, cedars, stone lanterns, a temple of dark wood. The city is quiet here.
🍵 A tea-house of modest appearance: rice, a little fish, tea in small cups, and girls in bright robes who bow as they pour.
THE LONG NOSES! · BATULCAR'S JAPANESE TROUPE
A shopkeeper of Yokohama
Welcome! An old robe for your fine coat? A good bargain, a good bargain.
Where to? The harbour, the temple, the circus?
WELLS, FARGO & CO.
HURRAH FOR CAMERFIELD!
The meeting in Montgomery Street
📣 Placards, banners, a crowd: "Hurrah for Camerfield!" "Mandiboy forever!" Nobody can say for what office.
A San Francisco newsboy
Paper! Paper! Election news! Camerfield or Mandiboy!
A miner back from the diggings
Struck it middlin' rich, mister. Middlin'.
The signal-man's hut
🚩 The signal-man of Medicine Bow, with his red flag: the bridge is shaky, he has telegraphed for a relief train.
The plains of Nebraska
Fort Kearney station
🚉 A wooden station on the open plain, its stove red-hot; the soldiers of the fort crowding the platform; the snow coming down.
The gate of Fort Kearney
🏰 A stockade of logs, blockhouses at the corners, barracks inside, the flag; a hundred soldiers of the United States Army, and a captain who must keep the fort.
🛷 A sort of frame on two long beams, a little raised in front like a sledge's runners; room for five or six; a high mast, a great brigantine sail, a jib, and a rudder behind.
A soldier of Fort Kearney
Cold enough to freeze a whistle, sir.
OMAHA · UNION PACIFIC
🚉 Omaha: the Union Pacific begins here, and from here the Chicago and Rock Island runs east every day. A train is ready to start.
CUNARD LINE · PIER No. 50
⚓ Pier 50, the Cunard line. The China, for Liverpool, left at a quarter before nine. Her smoke is still on the river.
The Henrietta, at her moorings
⚓ The Henrietta: a trading steamer with a screw, iron hull, wooden upper works, her funnel puffing smoke. Bound for Bordeaux.
The China? Gone, sir. Three-quarters of an hour ago.
🕰️ Twenty minutes before noon, the 21st of December. London is six hours away by the express.
A Liverpool docker
Mind your back, sir! Cotton from New Orleans, coming through.
The whist table in the saloon
🃏 Mr Fogg's rubber: four players, not a word more than the game needs. The thirty-third rubber of the voyage, or the fortieth.
The engine-room skylight
look down at the engines
🔥 Down below, the furnaces roar, the great cranks go round, the screw drives her on; the stokers' shovels flash in the glare.
The stair to the bridge
go up onto the bridge
⚓ The bridge. The officer of the watch, the helmsman, the compass; the whole sea ahead.
The way down from the bridge
go down to the deck
read the noon position
📋 The noon position, chalked on the board: latitude, longitude, and the miles run since yesterday. Mr Fogg reads it every day, and enters it in his book.
🌊 Spray, the stem cutting the sea, porpoises playing under the bow; far ahead, a smudge of smoke from another ship.
🌅 The sea, going by: a long swell, flying fish, a sail far off.
Down the gangway onto the quay.
⚓ The steamer. An iron screw steamer of the line: two masts, a tall funnel, the saloon aft, the whole sea round her.
The Peninsular Company's iron screw steamer, two thousand eight hundred tons, five hundred horse-power, Suez to Bombay.
The Peninsular Company's Rangoon, Calcutta to Hong Kong by Singapore: as fast as the Mongolia, not as comfortable.
The Peninsular Company's Carnatic, Hong Kong to Yokohama.
The Pacific Mail Company's General Grant: a great paddle-wheel steamer of two thousand five hundred tons, with three masts, Yokohama to San Francisco.
Out into the square, the sun white on the walls.
🏛️ The British consulate, Suez. A cool, high room with a slow fan: the consul's desk, his seal, the Queen's portrait, a window on the square.
The door to the square
🖋️ The consul's desk: passports to sign, the seal of the consulate, a list of the steamers due, and Mr Fix's telegram form, half filled in.
The window on the square
🪟 The square: palms, camels, white walls; two hundred steps off, the quay and the Mongolia.
Down the steps of Malabar Hill, the city below.
🛕 The pagoda on Malabar Hill. Carved pillars, lamps, flowers; worshippers come barefoot, as the custom is. The priests keep the sanctuary.
The door to the hill
look, from a respectful distance
🪔 The inner shrine, behind its carved doorway: lamps, flowers, the smell of incense. Only the priests go further.
The place for shoes
👞 Here, by the door, every worshipper leaves his shoes: it is forbidden to enter a temple shod. The English government itself has a law that its subjects must respect the religions of the country.
the railway carriage
Down onto the platform.
🚂 The railway carriage. The long car of the express: seats either side of the aisle, the stove, the windows; the country rolling by.
🔥 A cast-iron stove, red-hot; the conductor feeds it with coal from a box. Outside, the wind.
🃏 A little folding table between two seats: cards, counters, a pencil and the score.
The door to the platform
go out onto the platform
🌬️ The little open platform at the end of the car: the rails flying away behind, the wind enough to take your hat.
The carriage window
❄️ Snow, a white plain to the horizon, the telegraph poles going by.
🦬 Prairie and mountains; once, a herd of buffaloes crossing the line.
🌴 Palms and paddy-fields, villages, temples, a river; a tiger, perhaps, in the jungle.
Out under the trees: the glade, the torches, the dark.
🌙 The pagoda of Pillaji, by night. Torches guttering; the priests' guards at the doors; in an inner room, the young widow, drugged with the fumes of opium and hemp.
The door to the glade
The back wall of the pagoda
🧱 Brick and timber, the mortar soft with age. A way could be made through it, quietly, with a knife.
🌙 A young woman of great beauty lies there, senseless: the priests have drugged her with opium and hemp, so that she will not resist at dawn.
🌙 A young woman lies there, asleep: the priests have given her something to make her sleep. At dawn they mean to take her life. You mean to save her.
The guards at the door
🗡️ The rajah's guards, their swords drawn, watching by the torches. These ones are not asleep.
the court-house, Calcutta
Out into the street: the heat, the crowd, the river.
⚖️ The court-house, Calcutta. A high whitewashed hall; the judge's bench under a big clock; the dock; Europeans and natives crowding the back.
The door to the street
The big clock over the judge
🕰️ The big clock over the judge: its hands seem to go round with terrible rapidity. The steamer for Hong Kong leaves at noon.
🪵 The prisoners' dock: a wooden pen, its rail worn smooth.
📜 The clerk's table: the charge-sheet, the Bible, and a bundle tied in cloth: the evidence.
a tavern on the quay, Hong Kong
Out onto the quay: lanterns, the harbour, the night.
🏮 A tavern on the quay. A long room hung with lanterns; tables, benches, a counter of bottles; at the far end, a dim room behind a curtain, where men lie on couches.
The door to the quay
The curtain to the back room
💨 The back room: couches, a sweet heavy smoke, men lying in a stupor with long pipes beside them. Opium: forbidden in China, and sold in Hong Kong.
💨 The back room: couches in a dim haze of smoke, men lying asleep. Not a good place.
🍶 The counter: port, gin, brandy, rice wine, and the tavern-keeper polishing a glass, watching everyone.
Ashore, on the wharf of the pilot-boats.
⛵ The Tankadere, pilot-boat No. 43. Twenty tons, sharp as a racing yacht; two masts, a cloud of sail; John Bunsby and four men; one little cabin.
🛏️ The one little cabin: two cots, a lamp, a locker; Fix lies on one, saying nothing.
🧭 The tiller: John Bunsby's own place. He lets you hold her a moment, steady, steady.
The bow of the Tankadere
🌊 She leaps like a fish through the swell. Far ahead, the coast of China.
💥 A little brass gun, for signals in fog. And for other signals, if needed.
Batulcar's circus, Yokohama
Out into the street of the Japanese town.

🎪 The Honourable William Batulcar's troupe. Benches round a stage hung with paper lanterns; drums, flutes, a gong; jugglers, tumblers, a top spinning on a fan; and the Long Noses, under the patronage of the god Tingou.
🔔 BONG. The whole troupe looks round.
🎭 The stage: drums and flutes, a juggler with lighted candles, and the great act still to come: the Long Noses' pyramid.
👺 Wings of painted paper, noses of bamboo five, six, ten feet long, in a rack; costumes; a cat asleep in a basket.
Down the gangway onto the pier.
⚓ The Henrietta. An iron-hulled trading steamer, wooden upper works, two masts, one tall funnel; Captain Andrew Speedy's own, bound for Bordeaux. Or so he thinks.
🔥 The stokehold: the furnaces roaring white, the stokers black with coal dust. The bunker is nearly empty.
The Henrietta's wheel
🧭 Mr Fogg's course: east-north-east, for Liverpool. Not Bordeaux.
The captain's cabin
listen at the door
🔒 From inside, a furious voice, kicks at the door, and words that cannot be written down. Captain Speedy is locked in his cabin.
the Custom House, Liverpool
Out onto the quay, in the rain.
🏛️ The Custom House, Liverpool. A great hall of columns and a dome; clerks at their desks; at the back, a strong room with a barred window: the lock-up.
The door of the lock-up
🔒 The door of the lock-up, a grille in it. Inside: a bench, a barred window, and the rain.
The Custom House clock
🕰️ The clock of the Custom House. Every tick, a second Mr Fogg cannot spend.
THE SUEZ CANAL, 1869
Wednesday, October 2nd, at 8.45 p.m.
Thursday, October 3rd, at 7.20 a.m.
Turin, by Mont Cenis
Friday, October 4th, at 6.35 a.m.
Saturday, October 5th, at 4 p.m.
Wednesday, October 9th, at 11 a.m.
Fix. Agent of the Peninsular Company. At your service.
Good day. Mr Fogg is very kind to let me travel with him.
Sir Francis Cromarty
Good day to you. India is a great country; you will see a little of it.
In which a Conversation Takes Place which Seems Likely to Cost Phileas Fogg Dear
The memorandum of the wager
The Reform Club, Pall Mall: Wednesday, the 2nd of October 1872, the evening

Mr Fogg has walked from Saville Row to the Reform Club, as he does every day: five hundred and seventy-five steps of his right foot, five hundred and seventy-six of his left. He has dined, read the papers, and now sits down to whist with five other members.
Eighty days! I have the Telegraph's figures here.
Calm yourself, my dear Stuart. It's only a joke.
Well, what about that robbery?
Go through into the card room, where Mr Fogg's table is laid for whist
The talk tonight is of the great robbery at the Bank of England. Ask Thomas Flanagan what is known.
"Well, Ralph," said Thomas Flanagan, "what about that robbery?"
"Oh," replied Stuart, "the Bank will lose the money."
A package of banknotes, fifty-five thousand pounds, taken from the principal cashier's table three days ago, by a well-dressed gentleman of polished manners.
Gauthier Ralph, of the Bank of England
Gauthier Ralph is a director of the Bank. Ask him what is being done.
"In the first place, he is no robber at all," returned Ralph, positively.
🏦 A gentleman thief
A clerk of the Bank
Nobody at the Bank saw any clerk do it.
